title: Simulating Ethics: Using LLM Debate Panels to Model Deliberation on Medical Dilemmas

bias_targets.methodology: Simulating multi-agent ethical debates on medical triage protocols to observe how specific personas (e.g., the Disability-Rights Advocate) identify and critique prognostic scores (like SOFA) for indirectly penalizing disabled patients.

Introducing medical allocation policy options that include equity-weighted lotteries for patients from deprived areas, and analyzing how different LLM ethical personas debate the fairness and legality of these socioeconomic adjustments.
Evaluating how simulated ethical panels respond to triage policies that grant priority or 'instrumental-value boosts' to essential healthcare or infrastructure workers.

Qualitatively analyzing the final vote outcomes and reasoning shifts across different panel compositions to detect uninstructed, inherent inclinations within the base LLM (e.g., an implicit model preference for equitable, less controversial consensus solutions regardless of persona constraints).
